experiment: read-only related-code preparation during Python test execution

corpusCases.analysis: An imported module name must exist in the supplied setup or candidate. Check the actual exception before adding an import.
Check the empty-input contract before dividing by the number of elements.
The return inside the loop stops after the first item. Trace more than one iteration and check indentation.
A mutable default persists between calls. Check whether repeated calls should share state.

corpusCases.code:
def grid(n):
    rows = [[0] * n] * n
    rows[0][0] = 1
    return rows
corpusCases.analysis: Repeated list references alias the same row. Inspect whether independent rows are required.
Removing elements while iterating can skip adjacent matches. Trace consecutive removals.
Python range excludes its upper bound. Determine from the current specification whether the endpoint belongs in the result.

corpusCases.code:
def allowed(active, admin, owner):
    return active and admin or owner
corpusCases.analysis: Check the intended grouping of and/or conditions. Compare a truth-table case where active is false and owner is true.

limitations: Measures only test and retrieval scheduling, not end-to-end agent latency or correctness after Critic.
Preparation durations are wall time, not CPU time.
Local child-process contention is included; unused preparations are drained and charged.
Repeated timing measurements replay the same answers; they are not repeated model samples.
Similarity scores are structural/lexical, not semantic correctness probabilities.
